reviews.review:
Really awesome game if you find the right servers.
I prefer the roleplay servers tho :D
Love it !! Don't have it? Get it!!!

Terribly optimized graphics engine, but still VERY fun to play. High frame rates aren't too necessary in this game, because your typical encounter is a much more realistic than BF4 distance, which is usually 300m or more. Since bullets actually kill fast (like in real life) when hits are scored, close quarters encounters are short and deadly (clearing a building is actually dangerous unlike BF or CoD), and usually there's no lateral tracking to be done since people move slow compared to the absurdly unrealistic BF or CoD games. So 24 fps actually is quite playable in Arma 3 (I can play GTA V on near ultra settings on 1080p at 110 fps, to give you an idea of how poorly Arma 3's graphics are optimized).

As for gameplay, the game has a great story mode, and awesome multiplayer. Dogfights in jets aren't the stupid 60 mph dogfights like in BF4, but rather you're doing 300-400 mph while trying to stay on his tail. I've actually damaged my plane (and pilot) taking a nearly 9-G turn to dodge 4 incoming missiles after I ran out of flares (yes, aircraft have realistic quantities of ammo and fuel, as they should). If you plan to fly anything, you MUST have a mic, and most servers require Teamspeak (which is lame, since the game already has global, side, command, group, and vehicle channels, along with direct communications (proxy voice). There is no need for TS, unless if you're a brain-dead moron who doesn't know how to utilize the in-game channels. However, you will find yourself short of servers to play on if you don't respect the admins, most of whom play nothing but Arma 3, and have a God complex. Stroke their fragile egos, and all will be well for you.

Weapons aren't balanced, which is nice because they aren't balanced in real life. In real life, weapons are designed to be the best at the role they were meant for, and that's how the weapons in Arma 3 are coded. the only "balancing" is the weight penalties. Ammo for a .50 cal or 12.7mm AMR is freaking heavy in real life, and so it is in Arma 3. If you want to be a sniper using those big guns to score 1-shot-kills from 2 Km away, you can, but if you weigh yourself down with ammo, you will become easily fatigued, and your movement will be dropped to movement slower than an over-encumbered Elder Scrolls character. That brings us to the map size of the most popular map, Altis. Altis is big. B-I-G BIG. [url=http://40.media.tumblr.com/007afaa34183f95b41624c4719361748/tumblr_ms4vswcJ1c1rdy5joo1_1280.png]HERE[/url] is a to-scale illustration of Altis compared to other well-known large maps. I used to try to describe Battlefield maps to CoD players by saying an entire CoD map would fit into a BF home base. Well, Caspian Border fits nicely into the NATO air base on Altis. The little island-like peninsula on the southern part of Altis is just a bit smaller than Skyrim. Yeah, Altis is big. 270 square kilometers of land (167.77 square miles), and a total playable area that supports gameplay on land, air, sea, and under water of 1,000 square kilometers (621.37 square miles), making Altis bigger than FUEL's map. Yeah... it's bigger than FUEL. 'Nuff said.

So I'm getting bored of typing this, so I'll wrap up with saying this game is awesome if you like huge open-world simulators that openly supports modding. Speaking of which, there is a Hao mod. That's right, you can play Halo in Arma 3. I know you can play as ODSTs and UNSC marines, but I'm not sure about Spartans and Covenant, as I only just got the game and I haven't tried the mods yet. I give this game a 8/10, loosing 2 points due to graphic limitations.
